Nidhi Gupta, J.

Present appeal has been filed by the injured/claimant seeking enhancement of compensation of Rs.59,036/- granted by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Palwal (hereinafter referred to as "the learned Tribunal") vide Award dated 16.12.2015 passed in MVA Petition No.RBT- 76 of 2014 filed under Sections 166 and 140 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act").

2. Brief facts of the case are that the learned Tribunal on the basis of pleadings and evidence adduced before it concluded that the appellant/injured-claimant had suffered injuries in a motor vehicular accident that took place on 04.07.2013 due to rash and negligent driving of motorcycle bearing registration No.HR-50C-6898 (hereinafter referred to as 'the offending vehicle'), being driven by respondent No.1, owned by respondent No.2, and insured by respondent No.3.
Learned Tribunal awarded compensation as above along with interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of filing the claim petition till realisation.
1 of 5 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:071913 3.

Learned counsel for the appellant seeks enhancement of compensation on the grounds:
a) that the appellant has suffered multiple grievous and serious injuries on her body as a result of which she remained admitted in hospital for a considerable length of time and was advised further follow up treatment also.
It is submitted that it was proven on record that a special attendant had been engaged for the appellant.

sentences.text: It is prayed that accordingly, in view of the above facts, compensation awarded to the appellant be enhanced.
4. No other argument is raised on behalf of the appellant.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the appellant.
2 of 5 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:071913 6.

Perusal of impugned Award shows that it has been recorded therein that according to the MLR (Exhibit P1), the appellant had suffered following injuries:
"1. An abrasion (+) over right arm about 2 cms above elbow joint.
2. Tenderness (+) over right knee.
3. Complaint of pain over right side lower ribs.
4. Complaint of generalised osteopenia.
5. Complaint of pain in the lower back.
Petitioner has also produced X-ray reports Ex.P10 to Ex.P12.
X-ray pelvis with both hips A.P. View (Ex.P10) shows fractures of right superior and interior pubic rami with generalised osteopenia, X

-ray both knee joints AP &Lat views (Ex.P11) shows that moderate changes of osteoarthritis both knee joints with generalised osteopenia and X-ray Lumbo Sacral spine AP &Lat views (Ex.P12) shows grade I spondylolisthesis of L5 over S1 vertebral body with lumbar spondylosis with generalised osteopenia."

sentences.text: Perusal of above injuries shows that none of the injuries suffered by the appellant in the accident in question are serious or grievous in nature.

Admittedly, the appellant was about 60 years of age at the time of accident, and perusal of the above medical record shows that in fact, the appellant appears to be suffering largely from age-related osteopenia.
8. As per the record, the appellant had remained hospitalised from 04.07.2013 to 14.07.2013 and had also taken some subsequent treatment.
The appellant had produced medical bills to the 3 of 5 Neutral Citation No:=2023:PHHC:071913 tune of Rs.34,036/- which was spent by her on her medicines and treatment.
Said amount was duly reimbursed by the learned Tribunal.
9. Though it was the pleaded case of the appellant that she was earning Rs.5,000/- from tailoring work.
However, no proof of such income was produced by the appellant.

As such, learned Tribunal had taken her notional income as Rs.5,000/- per month as that of an unskilled labourer; and as the appellant remained hospitalised from 04.07.2013 to 14.07.2013 i.e. for a period of 10 days, and also underwent subsequent treatment from various hospitals, learned Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.5,000/- under the head of loss of income.
I find no error whatsoever in the said amount as, as per the appellant's own case she was earning Rs.5,000/- per month from tailoring work.
In the present case although the appellant remained hospitalised for a period of 10 days only, yet, the learned Tribunal has awarded Rs.5,000/- towards loss of income.
10. The appellant has admitted that she has suffered no permanent disability in the accident in question nor has any document been produced by her in this regard.
In view of above facts, an amount of Rs.10,000/- for pain & suffering; Rs.5,000/- for special diet and Rs.5,000/- for conveyance charges, is just and fair.

Compensation granted to the appellant by learned Tribunal is as follows in tabular form:-
Heads Amounts Medicines & medical treatment Rs.34,036/-
Loss of earnings during the Rs.5,000/-
period of treatment  4 of 5  Neutral Citation No:=2023:P  Loss of future earnings on Nil  account of permanent disability  Pain & suffering loss of amenities Rs.10,000/-
 of life  Conveyance & special diet Rs.10,000/-
 (Rs.5,000/- + Rs.5,000/-)
 Total Rs.59,036/-
